newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Chernomyrdin says crop outlook very good.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Chernomyrdin says crop outlook very good.

text.p: Russian prime minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, said on Thursday that the outlook for the domestic grain crop this year was very good.
"I don't remember a year when there weren't problems with the harvest -- there are some today, and not just a few," he told a cabinet meeting. "But the prospects for the harvest are especially good."
He did not provide a specific output forecast, but he did say average per-hectare yields had risen to 2.5-2.6 tonnes.
The government has forecast the grain crop flat at at least 70 million tonnes, but some officials have said net output could rise to 75-80 million tonnes.
Last year's outcome of 69.3 million tonnes was the second poor result in a row and one of the worst harvests on record in three decades.
